facts.raw_span: A 35-year-old man presented for routine follow‐up 11 years after a left total hip arthroplasty with a ceramic‐on‐ceramic articulation
left buttock and greater trochanteric pain
he denied fevers or systemic symptoms
range of motion of the left hip was full and painless
focal tenderness over the posterior buttock and greater trochanter but no palpable mass
Anteroposterior radiographs of the pelvis and left hip were unchanged compared with images obtained 1 year earlier
a diagnosis of greater trochanteric bursitis was made
an intra‐bursal corticosteroid injection was administered, resulting in partial symptom relief
persistent buttock pain and intermittent electric shock–like sensations radiating down the left leg
decreased and painful range of motion of the left hip
erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 22 mm/h
a left periprosthetic soft‐tissue mass measuring 9 × 8 × 10 cm, without bony involvement or bone‐marrow edema
